legs.target: CTO condition: print the transcripts key ARN beside the request_compositions key ARN
legs.proof_required: they must DIFFER; equal is a STOP
legs.proof: THE TWO KEYS DIFFER, MEASURED LIVE AT BOTH GRAINS OF THE request_compositions STORE. TRANSCRIPTS KEY (the key aws_kms_grant.commentary at commentary.tf:267 grants Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/DescribeKey on): arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:313476888478:key/44a2284f-1e14-4ea1-b6cb-f6121bfde35a, read live by `kms describe-key --key-id alias/opal-data-transcripts` (the alias aws_kms_alias.transcripts mints at main.tf:173, alias/${local.bucket}), description "Encrypts every object in the Opal meeting-transcripts bucket. Use is granted to named readers only." REQUEST_COMPOSITIONS STORE KEY: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:313476888478:key/7f4d3042-10d8-49a7-b55e-3c963cea8111. The condition names one key but the store has TWO grains and the half's purpose (its lines 20-21: the grant does not reopen msg 2341 only if the transcripts key does not encrypt request_compositions) is only answered by reading both, so both were read: (i) DynamoDB -- `describe-table --table-name irpt-requests` (the table every request_compositions policy addresses as data.terraform_remote_state.core.outputs.tables.requests) reads SSEType KMS, Status ENABLED, KMSMasterKeyArn 7f4d3042-10d8-49a7-b55e-3c963cea8111; (ii) S3 -- the irpt PRODUCT bucket, resolved FROM THE LGIC REGISTRY and never typed (infra/logic/registry/scopes.json, key irpt, class PRODUCT -> opal-data-irpt, the same derivation ops/iam.tf:134 uses so the grant and the address cannot name different buckets), reads a default of SSEAlgorithm aws:kms with KMSMasterKeyID 7f4d3042-10d8-49a7-b55e-3c963cea8111, which is where the state/request_compositions family lands. BOTH GRAINS RESOLVE TO THE SAME KEY AND NEITHER IS THE TRANSCRIPTS KEY: 44a2284f != 7f4d3042. So the transcripts key does not encrypt request_compositions, the commentary grant is confined to the transcripts stack's own key for its queues and logs, and msg 2341's prohibition on kms:Decrypt over IRPT's request_compositions is not reopened by it. No STOP. Note on the instrument: this is an EXISTENCE-AND-EQUALITY read of two live key ARNs, not an IAM simulation -- the simulator's verdicts are leg SIM's, and a key-policy-only grant reads implicitDeny there, so the key policy is read where the simulator is blind as the order requires.

legs.target: CTO condition: simulate as the commentary role
legs.proof_required: dynamodb:GetItem and kms:Decrypt on the IRPT table/key DENIED; lambda:InvokeFunction on the reader and the store ALLOWED. A key-policy-only grant reads implicitDeny in the simulator, so the KEY POLICY is read where the simulator is blind -- the TO-RUN-a17 finding this order cites back to me
legs.proof: THE FOUR VERDICTS ARE ESTABLISHED, BUT NOT BY THE SIMULATOR -- AND THAT SUBSTITUTION IS THE FIRST THING A READER NEEDS. iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy IS NOT AVAILABLE TO THIS DEVICE'S PRINCIPAL: the call returns AccessDenied, "User: arn:aws:iam::313476888478:user/cloudops-dell2-agent-user is not authorized to perform: iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy on resource: arn:aws:iam::313476888478:role/outlook-global-commentary-draft-role because no identity-based policy allows the iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy action". So the step-5 instrument the order names DID NOT RUN on this device and NO simulate verdict is claimed. What follows is the POLICY-DOCUMENT read, which for an absent permission is the stronger evidence anyway: a simulate returns implicitDeny for a missing grant, a typo, a conditioned statement and a wrong-grain ARN alike, whereas the statement set either contains the action or it does not. THE DENOMINATOR IS PRINTED AND THE VERDICTS ARE TAKEN BY SUBTRACTION FROM IT, never by a forward guess: the role carries ZERO inline policies (list-role-policies returns an empty list) and EXACTLY THREE attached managed policies -- outlook-global-commentary-draft-policy, irpt-commentary-composition-invoke-policy, irpt-commentary-draft-store-invoke-policy, which are the three attachments the COO half lists and nothing more -- whose default versions hold NINE statements in total: (1) s3:GetObject on opal-data-transcripts/outlook/transcripts/gold/*; (2) secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on astn/kimi/api-key-*; (3) secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on opal/ticketing/svc-commentary-*; (4) logs:CreateLogStream and logs:PutLogEvents on its OWN log group only; (5) sqs:ReceiveMessage, DeleteMessage and GetQueueAttributes on its analysis-ready queue; (6) sqs:SendMessage on its own DLQ; (7) sqs:SendMessage on the commentary-ready queue; (8) lambda:InvokeFunction on irpt-commentary-composition-read-lambda; (9) lambda:InvokeFunction on irpt-commentary-draft-store-lambda. VERDICT 1, dynamodb:GetItem on the request_compositions table (irpt-requests): DENIED. Not one of the nine statements names ANY dynamodb action, so the implicit deny stands by subtraction from the printed nine. VERDICT 2, kms:Decrypt on IRPT's key 7f4d3042-10d8-49a7-b55e-3c963cea8111: DENIED, and read from BOTH sides because an identity-policy read alone cannot see a key-policy grant. Identity side: not one of the nine statements names ANY kms action. Key-policy side, which is exactly where the simulator is blind: the IRPT key's policy is 291 bytes and holds ONE statement, Sid "Enable IAM User Permissions", Principal AWS arn:aws:iam::313476888478:root, Action kms:*, Resource * -- the default delegation to IAM, so access to that key is governed entirely by identity policies and there is no key-policy-side grant to any named role; 0 occurrences of outlook-global-commentary-draft in it. A CONTROL CORRECTION WORTH RECORDING: the first pass at that check grepped for the pattern AWS-colon-space-quote and matched nothing, which would have made a 291-byte REAL policy look like an empty or failed read and turned a broken pattern into a verdict. The file was printed rather than trusted: the policy renders the key as AWS-space-colon-space-quote, so the pattern was wrong, not the read. An emptiness that carries a verdict gets a control. VERDICT 3, lambda:InvokeFunction on the READER irpt-commentary-composition-read-lambda: ALLOWED by statement 8, resource-scoped to that one function ARN. VERDICT 4, lambda:InvokeFunction on the STORE irpt-commentary-draft-store-lambda: ALLOWED by statement 9, resource-scoped to that one function ARN. SO MSG 2341'S LINE HOLDS AS BUILT: the drafter reaches IRPT data through IRPT's own reader and store by invoke only, and holds no IRPT S3, DynamoDB or KMS grant of its own. THE TRANSCRIPTS KEY IS A GRANT, NOT A POLICY, which is the other thing a simulator cannot see: kms list-grants on 44a2284f-1e14-4ea1-b6cb-f6121bfde35a returns EXACTLY ONE grant for this role -- id b36d802cf2844bad5a343812a8c6e42e2bb8ce55f5ee9897da566733c01bdb9a, name outlook-global-commentary-draft-role, operations exactly Decrypt, GenerateDataKey and DescribeKey, the three commentary.tf declares and no fourth. OWED ELSEWHERE AND NAMED RATHER THAN QUIETLY REPLACED: the simulate itself, run on a device whose principal holds iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy.
